en: The *Śāradāṣṭaka Stotra*: I praise her whose beautiful body resembles a conch shell, the moon, the kunda flower, and snow; who is seated upon a swan, and whose splendor is as radiant as a lotus petal.
I perpetually bow to the blessed goddess Śāradā, whose gentle form is adorned with divine garments and ornaments. || 1 ||
She who ferries across the great ocean of the sea of saṃsāra those beings submerged within it; she whose lotus-feet are worshipped by gods and men;
her limbs adorned with necklaces, half-necklaces, jewels, and earrings.
I perpetually bow to the Blessed Lady, the illustrious Śāradā. || 2 ||
She who is called Bhāratī is the mother in this world of those people shattered by the heavy darkness of delusion;
she is celebrated by the sages whose every fault has been destroyed.
I perpetually bow to the Blessed Lady, the illustrious Śāradā. || 3 ||
Delighting in the playing of the lute, holding a crystal rosary and a golden book,
she is exquisitely beautiful with auspicious jewels, her lotus-like hands gracefully formed.
I perpetually bow down to the Blessed Lady, the illustrious Śāradā. || 4 ||
One's mother is always to be honored, the hosts of goddesses are to be saluted, and they are to be fully delighted in the mind; likewise,
one who desires life should offer praise for virtues and bring forth the fruits [of merit].
I perpetually bow to the blessed Śrī Śāradā. || 5 ||
He who, having bowed, worships the renowned Mother in this world, shall indeed always attain the fivefold happiness from the Blessed Lady—
becoming a possessor of beauty, form, virtue, wealth, and excellent enjoyments.
I perpetually bow to the blessed goddess Śrī Śāradā. || 6 ||

The hosts of the Goddess and others, with their beautiful lotus-faces, should be fully worshipped with offerings, oblations, and sacrifices; for by those who have worshipped her, the Blessed One— who indeed destroys dullness— is truly honored.
I perpetually bow to the blessed goddess Śrī Śāradā. || 7 ||
Having attained the grace of her who bestows happiness,
one becomes equal in splendor to the sun risen by the Lord of the Three Worlds;
she is the giver of the fruits of dharma, artha, and kāma, and furthermore, the giver of liberation.
I perpetually bow down to the blessed goddess Śrī Śāradā. || 8 ||
The Śrīśāradāṣṭakastotra is completed.
